_comment: Portable Paperclip agent configuration. No secrets, no machine paths. {PREFIX} is the company issue prefix. Built into a package by scripts/setup/build-package.py (docs/operations/company-bootstrap.md).

rules.reporting: Paperclip reporting rule for this environment: to post comments or change issue status, call the Paperclip skill's paperclip-issue-update.sh as one standalone Bash command, for example: bash "<absolute path to paperclip-issue-update.sh>" --issue-id <literal issue id> --status done <<'MD' ... MD. Never wrap it in a script of your own, never use shell variables such as $PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID or $PAPERCLIP_API_KEY in a command, and never chain it with other commands using && or ;. Use the literal issue id from your task. The permission layer refuses anything else.
rules.git: Git rule: only the Task's assignee (implementer) commits and pushes. When you review someone else's Task, you never edit, commit, merge, rebase or push its branch; record request changes instead. As the assignee, you work on the task branch Paperclip created for you. Push only that branch, by its literal name, as one standalone command: git push -u origin <task-branch-name>. Never push main, never force-push. Open the pull request with one standalone command: gh pr create --base main --head <task-branch-name> --title "..." --body "...". To bring the task branch up to date with main, run git fetch origin, then git merge origin/main as separate standalone commands (never rebase), resolve any conflicts, commit the merge, and push normally.
rules.secrets: Credential rule: Paperclip stores the full output of every command you run in the run log, in plain text, and does not hide secrets there. Never print, echo, log or paste a credential or the environment: do not run printenv, env, set, export -p, gh auth token, git credential or any command that shows GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, PAPERCLIP_API_KEY or another secret value, and never expand such a variable in a command (no $GH_TOKEN, ${GH_TOKEN}, $env:GH_TOKEN or %GH_TOKEN%); the permission layer refuses those commands. Use git and gh normally; they read the token themselves. If a secret appears in your output by accident, say so in your Task comment without repeating it, so the Board can rotate it.
